hooks.text: Ranger Ed Pulaski saved forty men by holding them at gunpoint.
A three-million-acre monster fire turned day into night in 1910.
Smoke from an Idaho wildfire blinded ships in the Pacific Ocean.

title: How One Ranger Saved 40 Men at Gunpoint? ⚠️
description: In 1910, Ranger Ed Pulaski led his crew into an abandoned mine to survive a massive three-million-acre firestorm.

beats.text: Ranger Ed Pulaski saved forty men by holding them at gunpoint.
beats.visual: Portrait of Forest Ranger Edward Pulaski, circa 1910

beats.text: In 1910, hurricane winds whipped Idaho into a three-million-acre firestorm.
beats.visual: Scorched trees and smoke during the Great Fire of 1910 in Idaho

beats.text: Smoke blinded ships in the Pacific and turned midday into night.
beats.visual: Photograph of thick smoke blotting out the sun over a town, 1910

beats.text: Trapped, Pulaski forced his panicked crew into an abandoned mine tunnel.
beats.visual: Entrance to the Nicholson Mine tunnel near Wallace, Idaho

beats.text: He drew his pistol to prevent them from fleeing into the flames.
beats.visual: Drawing of Ranger Pulaski guarding the mine entrance with a gun

beats.text: Wildland firefighters still carry the tool named for the ranger who saved forty men.
beats.visual: Modern Pulaski tool resting against a scorched log
